conversation.content:
Hello! My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you're here today, and I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently. Becoming a new mother can be a life-altering experience, and it's completely normal to have a wide range of emotions during this time.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to get a better understanding of how you're feeling. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during the postpartum period. It's essential to remember that this assessment is not a diagnostic tool, but rather a way for us to have a more in-depth conversation about your emotional well-being.

Please know that everything we discuss today is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself. I want you to feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings with me, and I'm here to listen without judgment.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions, which we'll go through together. These questions will help us understand your emotional state over the past week, and they'll give us a better sense of how you're adjusting to motherhood. Don't worry; this is not a test, and there are no right or wrong answers. I'm simply here to support you and gather information to help us work together.

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been feeling happy and fulfilled, or have you been experiencing some difficulties?

.. to be honest, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but it's just been really hard to adjust to everything. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I get up, take care of the baby, try to eat and sleep when I can... but it all just feels so exhausting. And sometimes, when I'm alone with my thoughts, I start to worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is the baby safe? Am I doing everything right? It's like, my mind just starts racing, and I feel anxious and scared. 

And it's not just the baby stuff... I just feel really sad and discouraged a lot of the time. I look at my friends who seem to be handling motherhood so much better than me, and I feel like I'm just not measuring up. I feel guilty for feeling this way, like I should be happier and more grateful. But at the same time, I just feel so... lost, I guess. Like, I don't know who I am anymore, or what I'm supposed to be doing. It's all just really confusing and hard. 

I don't know if that makes sense... it's just, everything feels really overwhelming right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still try to find the humor in things, but it's just not coming as easily to me right now. I feel like I'm just so caught up in worrying about the baby and trying to take care of everything that I don't have the energy to laugh and joke like I used to. Sometimes, my husband will try to make me laugh, and I'll smile, but it's just not the same. It feels forced, you know? Like, I'm trying to be happy and carefree, but it's just not genuine.

I do still enjoy some things, like watching my baby sleep or seeing her little smile when she's happy. Those things still bring me joy, but it's not like it used to be. I used to love watching TV, reading books, and hanging out with friends, but now all of those things just feel like too much effort. I'd rather just sit on the couch and stare at the wall, which is really sad, because I know that's not healthy.

I guess what I'm saying is, I don't feel like myself right now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and I'm not really experiencing much pleasure or joy in my life. And that's hard for me, because I used to be a really happy and optimistic person.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

.. to be honest, not really. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like too much work. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or meeting a friend for coffee, just feel like too much effort. I'll think about doing something, and then I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the things I need to do to make it happen, like getting the baby dressed and fed, and finding someone to watch her... it just feels like too much.

And even when I do try to do something I enjoy, like reading a book or watching a movie, I just can't seem to focus. My mind starts wandering, and I'll think about all the things I need to do, or worry about the baby, and I just can't relax. It's like, I'm trying to enjoy myself, but my brain is just not cooperating.

I do look forward to some things, like my husband coming home from work, or my mom visiting to help with the baby. Those things give me something to look forward to, and they make me feel a little better. But overall, I just don't feel like I'm enjoying things like I used to. Everything just feels so hard and overwhelming, and it's hard to find the energy to look forward to things.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... this one really resonates with me. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not eating well, I think it's because I'm not making enough milk or that I'm not feeding her often enough. If she's not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not creating a good sleep environment or that I'm not establishing a good routine.

I even blame myself for things that aren't even my fault. Like, the other day, the baby had a blowout diaper, and I was like, "Oh, this is all my fault. I should have changed her diaper sooner." Or, if my husband is stressed out, I'll think, "This is all my fault. I'm not doing enough to help him or support him."

It's like, I'm always looking for ways to criticize myself and think about what I could be doing better. And it's exhausting, because it feels like I'm never good enough, no matter what I do. I feel like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, so I can blame myself for it.

Sometimes, my husband will try to reassure me and tell me that it's not my fault, but it's hard for me to shake off that feeling of guilt and self-blame. It's like, it's just always there, lurking in the back of my mind, waiting to pounce on me whenever something goes wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... this is something I've been experiencing a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if the baby chokes on something? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if the baby gets sick? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I feel like I'm on edge all the time.

And it's not just big things, either. I'll worry about little things, like what if I forget to buy diapers? What if I run out of formula? What if the baby doesn't like the food I'm making for her? It's like, my brain is just constantly coming up with new things to worry about, and it's exhausting.

Sometimes, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start worrying about everything. I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll feel like I'm going to have a panic attack or something. My heart will be racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to throw up. It's like, my body is just responding to all these worries and anxieties, even if they're not rational.

And the worst part is, I know that a lot of these worries are irrational. I mean, the baby is healthy, and I'm doing my best to take care of her. But it's hard to shake off that feeling of anxiety and worry. It's like, it's just always there, lurking in the back of my mind, waiting to pounce on me whenever I'm not expecting it.

Sometimes, I'll try to talk to my husband about it, and he'll just tell me to relax and that everything will be okay. But it's hard to relax when you're feeling so anxious and worried all the time. I just wish I could turn off my brain and just be calm for once.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... this is something that's been happening to me a lot lately. I'll be doing something normal, like feeding the baby or taking a shower, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like, my body is just responding to some kind of internal alarm, but I don't know what's triggering it.

Sometimes, it's when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the baby stops breathing? What if I'm not doing something right? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of fear and panic.

Other times, it's when I'm in a crowded place, like the grocery store or the park. I'll just feel like I'm trapped, and I'll start to feel anxious and panicky. I'll think about all the people around me, and I'll worry that someone is going to hurt me or the baby. It's like, my brain is just constantly on high alert, waiting for something bad to happen.

It's hard to explain, because it's not like I'm really scared of anything specific. It's just this general feeling of dread and anxiety that's always lurking in the back of my mind. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to happen.

Sometimes, I'll try to take some deep breaths and calm myself down, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic. It's like, my body is just responding to some kind of internal stress signal, and I don't know how to turn it off. It's really scary, because I feel like I'm losing control, and I don't know how to get back to feeling normal again.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's a definite yes. I feel like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to cook and clean and do laundry... it's all just so overwhelming. And on top of that, I'm trying to recover from the birth, and deal with all the physical and emotional changes that come with that. It's like, my body is still healing, but my mind is already racing ahead, trying to keep up with all the demands of motherhood.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, feeling like I'm doing okay, and then suddenly I'll just feel like I'm drowning. The baby will be crying, and the laundry will be piling up, and I'll just feel like I'm not doing enough. I'll think about all the things I need to do, and I'll just feel like I'm going to collapse under the weight of it all.

I try to prioritize, and make lists, and break things down into smaller tasks, but it's hard to keep up. And sometimes, I'll just feel like I'm failing, like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not good enough. It's like, I'm trying to be this perfect mother, but I'm just not measuring up.

My husband tries to help, and he's really supportive, but sometimes I feel like I'm a burden to him, too. Like, I'm just adding to his stress and his workload, and that's not fair to him. So, I try to do everything myself, and that just makes me feel even more overwhelmed.

It's like, I'm just trying to keep my head above water, but the waves just keep crashing down on me. And I don't know how to stop them, or how to catch my breath. I just feel like I'm constantly struggling to stay afloat, and it's exhausting.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. I mean, that's definitely part of it, but even when she's sleeping, I'll lie awake at night, feeling anxious and worried about everything.

I'll think about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and it just keeps me up. I'll feel like I'm wide awake, and my mind is just racing, and I don't know how to calm it down. Sometimes, I'll get out of bed and try to do something to distract myself, but nothing seems to work.

And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just so unsettling. I'll dream about the baby getting hurt, or about me not being able to take care of her, and it's just so realistic that it wakes me up, and I'm left feeling anxious and on edge.

It's like, my brain is just constantly working, even when I'm trying to sleep. And it's not just the baby that's keeping me up, it's my own thoughts and worries that are just swirling around in my head. I'll feel like I'm exhausted, but at the same time, I'll be wide awake, and I don't know how to turn it off.

Sometimes, I'll try to talk to my husband about it, but he'll just tell me to relax, and that everything will be okay. But it's hard to relax when you're feeling so anxious and overwhelmed all the time. I just wish I could find a way to calm my mind, and get some rest. I feel like I'm running on empty, and I don't know how much longer I can keep going like this.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I know I'm supposed to be happy and excited about being a new mom, but the truth is, I just feel really overwhelmed and unhappy most of the time.

I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. I don't even know why, it's just like this wave of sadness washes over me, and I feel like I'm drowning in it. Sometimes, it's because I'm thinking about all the things I used to be able to do, but can't do anymore. Like, I used to love going out with friends, or trying new restaurants, but now it's just so hard to leave the house with the baby.

Other times, it's because I'm feeling so guilty and anxious about everything. I'll think about all the things I'm not doing right, or all the things I'm not providing for the baby, and it just feels like this weight is crushing me. I'll feel like I'm a failure, and that I'm not good enough to be a mom.

It's hard, because I know I'm not alone in feeling this way. I've talked to other moms, and they've all said they've felt the same way at some point or another. But it's hard to remember that when you're in the midst of it, you know? It's hard to remember that it's okay to feel sad, and that it doesn't mean I'm a bad mom.

Sometimes, I'll try to put on a happy face, and pretend like everything is fine, but it's just so exhausting. I feel like I'm living this lie, and that I'm just waiting for someone to find out that I'm really struggling. It's hard to admit, but I just feel really sad and miserable most of the time, and I don't know how to make it stop.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's not even always about something specific, it's just like this overwhelming feeling of sadness and frustration that builds up inside me and then just bursts out in tears.

Sometimes, it's when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and anxious, like when the baby is crying and I don't know how to calm her down, or when I'm feeling really guilty about something, like not being able to breastfeed or not being able to get her to sleep. Other times, it's just when I'm feeling really lonely and isolated, like when my husband is at work and I'm stuck at home with the baby all day.

I'll try to hold it in, but sometimes it's just too much, and I'll just break down in tears. It's embarrassing, because sometimes my husband will be there, and he'll try to comfort me, but I just feel like I'm being so weak and emotional. I'll try to apologize and tell him it's okay, but deep down, I'm just feeling so overwhelmed and sad.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, but really, I'm just feeling really lost and scared. I'm trying to navigate all these new emotions and responsibilities, and it's just feeling really overwhelming. Sometimes, I'll cry because I'm just feeling so exhausted and drained, and I don't know how to keep going.

It's not always easy to talk about, but I guess it's just something I need to acknowledge, you know? I'm not okay, and that's okay. I'm struggling, and I need help. I just wish I could find a way to make the tears stop, and to feel like myself again.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I don't know how to talk about this, but... yes. The thought has occurred to me. It's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I want to admit, but it's the truth. When I'm feeling really overwhelmed and sad, and I don't know how to make it stop, sometimes I'll have these thoughts. They're not really thoughts, exactly, they're more like... impulses, I guess. Like, I'll be feeling so desperate and trapped, and I'll think, "What if I just...?"

It's not like I really want to hurt myself, it's just that the pain and the sadness feel so overwhelming, and I don't know how to make it stop. It's like, my brain is just trying to find a way to escape, you know? And sometimes, those thoughts will pop into my head, and it's like, I'll feel this wave of... I don't know, it's not exactly calm, but it's like, a sense of possibility, I guess. Like, maybe if I just did something to hurt myself, the pain would stop.

But it's not really like that, I know. I know that hurting myself wouldn't solve anything, and it would just make things worse. And I don't really want to hurt myself, I just... I don't know, I feel like I'm just so stuck, and I don't know how to get out of this place.

It's hard to talk about, because I feel like I'm being so weak, and I'm ashamed of myself. But at the same time, I know that I need to talk about it, because it's not okay to feel this way. And I need help, I know that. I just don't know how to ask for it, or what kind of help I need.

I guess what I'm trying to say is, yes, the thought has occurred to me. And it's scary, and it's not okay, and I don't know what to do about it. But I'm trying to be honest, and I'm trying to face it, because I know that's the only way I'll ever be able to get through this.
